title: Rewiring the Chronic Pain Experience: Single-Session Model of Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT) at The Ottawa Hospital
official: Rewiring the Chronic Pain Experience: Feasibility and Pilot Testing of a Single-Session, 4-Hour Delivery Model of Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT) at The Ottawa Hospital (TOH)
summary:
The goal of this study is to find out if a one-time session of Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT) intervention improves participant's mood and pain. Participants in this 4 hours session will be 40 patients who've been referred to the The Ottawa Hospital Pain Clinic (TOHPC) for chronic pain.

The main questions of this study are:

* Can we recruit 40 participants within 6 months?
* Do at least 32 participants complete the session and answer follow up questions?
* Does 1 session of PRT have a positive impact on participants' mood and pain?

Participants in this study will:

* Attend 1 session of PRT.
* Answer questions that relate to their experience of pain and their mood. They will answer these questions immediately before/after the session, 1 week after the session, and 1 month after the session.
* After the session, some participants will participate in an interview to talk about their experience.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Minimum age of 18 years or older at time of consent.
* Chronic pain persisting for a minimum of 3 months, consistent with the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) definition of chronic pain.
* Self-reported 1-week average pain intensity score between 4/10 and 9/10 on the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI)12 at screening.

  o Note: Individuals scoring less than 4/10 or more than 9/10 will be directed to other pain clinic workshops and available resources (e.g., Power Over Pain)
* Referred to TOHPC and triaged by a registered nurse, nurse practitioner, or physician to the "diffuse pain" pathway;
* Completed the initial pain clinic patient education and resource session (PERS) for patients triaged to the "diffuse pain" pathway;
* Currently waiting for a 1st consultation with the Nurse Practitioner assigned to the "diffuse pain" pathway.
* Able to read, write, and communicate in English at a level sufficient to engage with research team, the psychoeducational content, and to complete self-report measures.
* Able to attend a single, in-person 4-hour group session at TOHPC in Ottawa on a scheduled weekday.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Active mental health symptoms that significantly interfere with the ability to engage with psychoeducational content (e.g., dissociation, active psychosis), or participate in a group setting
* Cognitive impairment that significantly limits the ability to comprehend study information, provide informed consent, or meaningfully engage with psychoeducational content.
* Scheduled for a major surgical procedure within the study timeframe.
* Currently receiving other individual or group psychotherapy that directly targets pain, pain cognitions, or pain-related emotional responses within the 12 weeks prior to enrollment.
* Currently receiving interventional pain management services (e.g., injections, nerve blocks) from another clinic or institution within the 12-week period prior to enrollment through the 3-month follow-up.
